reason: E1 provides general evidence that boron improves grain boundary cohesion and cites prior work on fracture mode change, supporting the first premise. E2 and E3 directly report that 0.1 at.% boron in HfMoNbTaTiZr induces (Hf,Zr)B2 precipitation, enhances grain boundary cohesion, shifts fracture to transgranular, and improves ductility and strength, fully supporting premises 2-4. However, no cited evidence addresses the preservation of impact-induced energy release (premise 5), which is a key claim of the hypothesis.
premises: Boron addition improves grain boundary cohesion in alloys, changing fracture mode from intergranular to transgranular
0.1 at.% boron in HfMoNbTaTiZr induces intergranular (Hf,Zr)B2 precipitation
Boride precipitation enhances grain boundary cohesion, shifting fracture mode to transgranular
This microstructural change improves ductility and work hardenability without sacrificing strength
Impact-induced energy release characteristics are preserved after boron addition
